title: StellarPay renewal & regional scale sync
summary: Review of 12-month renewal options with a reserved capacity bump for EU region, discussion of latency SLAs and private deployment constraints, agreement to run a targeted benchmark and send a revised quote for exec approval.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-29 15:00 PT
Duration: 38 minutes
Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Lina (Redwood SE), Jason (CFO, StellarPay), Priya (Head of ML), Omar (Platform Lead), Elena (Legal)

Auto-summary (optional): Customer is approaching renewal, wants to expand reserved capacity and add EU region for PSD2 compliance. Main blockers: pricing, contractual SLAs, and KMS/data-residency controls. Agreed next steps: benchmark run, revised quote, legal review.

Transcript:
[00:00] Samir: hey everybody, thanks for joining, um this is Samir from Redwood - i'm the AE on the account, quick check, audio ok?
[00:06] Jason: yep, good here. thanks.
[00:08] Priya: hi, yeah we're good.
[00:10] Samir: cool. quick agenda, i'll recap renewal options, lina will walk through perf and private options, and then we can talk next steps. sound good?
[00:18] Omar: yep, go for it.
[00:20] Lina: all right thanks. so quick context - we know StellarPay is at ~6k requests per minute peak, most inference is payment-fraud models, any traffic that goes to eu needs to stay in eu datacenters. you mentioned you wanted a reserved pool plus a smaller private control plane?
[00:34] Jason: correct. we want to lock in capacity for traffic spikes, and add an eu region so european customers' data doesn't leave region.
[00:40] Priya: also lower p99 latency is important for user flow in checkout, we want consistent sub-200ms p99 if possible.
[00:48] Lina: got it. for sub-200 p99 we'll recommend a combination: reserved GPU pool (dedicated), prefix/KV caching for hot prompts, and model quantization where acceptable. caveat: cost goes up with reserved capacity but we can control it via config.
[01:05] Jason: do you have numbers? like if we double reserved slots what happens to latency and cost?
[01:10] Lina: yes, rough numbers from similar fintechs: doubling reserved GPUs drops p99 by ~30-40% on typical sequences, unit cost per token goes up by about 15-25% depending on utilization. we can run a targeted bench with your corpus to give exacts.
[01:25] Samir: to add, we can offer a 12-month contract with a tiered discount for committed throughput - we discussed a 12 month vs 24 month tradeoff in the doc. i'll put a formal quote after we pick capacity.
[01:36] Elena: legal quick point: for eu residency we need contract language about data not leaving the eu, plus KMS integration with our on-prem HSM. is that supported?
[01:45] Lina: yes, we support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM in Private deployments. if you want the control plane in your VPC that's also an option - note that onboarding time is longer for private.
[01:55] Omar: onboarding time — what's the delta? we have a maintenance window in mid-october we could use.
[02:01] Lina: private VPC install typically 4-6 weeks, on-prem can be 6-10 weeks depending on infra. Dedicated hosted eu region provisioning is faster, usually 7-10 days once commit is signed.
[02:14] Jason: hmm okay. we might need a short-term bridge — run in hosted eu while private is provisioned.
[02:20] Samir: that's common. we'll propose a phased rollout: provision dedicated eu capacity first, then migrate to private control plane if you go that route.
[02:28] Priya: one practical ask — can we run a throughput benchmark with our real requests? we need to validate p99 under encrypted payloads, and also check the K-V cash behavior.
[02:39] Lina: absolutely. small note the transcript might say K-V cash sometimes — its KV cache, but we'll note that in the bench plan. we'll need a scrubbed sample corpus and an account to run 24-hour load.
[02:50] Jason: we'll prepare. can you also show the cost delta if we enable auto-burst vs fixed reserved?
[02:56] Samir: yes, Lina can run sim cost models. we can show per-token math and a 12-month TCO.
[03:03] Lina: quick thing on SLAs — our Dedicated plan includes latency SLO targets; SLA credits are tied to availability, we can negotiate tighter p99 SLOs for enterprise agreements but that maps to higher commitment and a runbook for fallback.
[03:16] Elena: legal — what about audit logs and retention? we need 7 years for payments-related access logs in some scenarios.
[03:23] Samir: Redwood Console stores per-request traces and, with the enterprise retention add-on, we can hold logs per your retention policy. we'll include the specifics in the contract addendum.
[03:33] Priya: any friction with model variants? we run a couple of custom finetuned models and a base open model. seamless rollovers?
[03:40] Lina: yes, version pinning and rollouts are supported. if you want automatic fallback to a lower-cost variant we can configure that too. caveat: switching models can change latency/cost, so bench across variants.
[03:52] Jason: competitors — we did a quick pilot with another provider, they had lower list prices but much higher p99 and no EU private control plane. we want to be clear on cost vs latency tradeoff.
[04:05] Samir: understood. we try to quantify that in the quote and bench results.
[04:10] Omar: timeline sense — if we sign by mid-october can we have dedicated eu up by end of october?
[04:16] Lina: yes, signing by oct 15 would allow provision by oct 28-31 assuming capacity available. private will come later though.
[04:24] Jason: what about incident response and runbook access? we need a named escalation path and quarterly reviews.
[04:31] Samir: included in enterprise tier, we'll list pager contacts and a quarterly ops review cadence.
[04:37] Priya: a more technical note — our sequences are typically 120-180 tokens, with KV cache hits around 60% for session lookups. how will that impact effective throughput?
[04:48] Lina: with 60% KV hits you get major cost savings because cached prefixes don't incur full attention. effective throughput improves significantly. we'll call that out in the bench.
[04:57] Jason: ok. Elena — anything from legal side before we proceed?
[05:01] Elena: just need the draft with data residency clause and KMS/HSM specifics. and will route to procurement for the exec sig.
[05:08] Samir: we'll include both in the addendum.
[05:11] --- (skipping to bench logistics / pricing discussion) ---
[10:12] Lina: for the benchmark i propose: 24 hour soak at 120% of peak, a synthetic walk-through of checkout flows, and a cold-start burst test. we'll measure p50/p95/p99, tokens per second, and per-token cost.
[10:25] Priya: ok we'll provide a scrubbed dataset and a runbook for instrumentation.
[10:29] Lina: great. for the quote, if you commit to 12 months at X reserved gpus we can do a 17% discount off list; 24 months gets ~25%. i'll put both scenarios.
[10:38] Jason: can you do a 20% for 12 months? that's closer to our threshold.
[10:42] Samir: we can propose a middle ground — i'll ask finance for a 20% for 12 months if we include a 6-month review and a bench acceptance criteria.
[10:51] Jason: sounds fair.
[10:53] Lina: one more thing on monitoring — Redwood Console can export per-route telemetry to your Datadog/Prometheus. any preferences?
[10:59] Omar: datadog for infra, prometheus for internal. so both would be useful.
[11:04] Samir: noted. we'll include config notes.
[11:07] Elena: data deletion — can we have API-controlled deletion triggers? our legal says we need the ability to remove certain cohorts on request.
[11:15] Lina: yes, data deletion APIs and retention policies are available, and we can support e-discovery scoping.
[11:21] --- (wrap up) ---
[36:10] Samir: quick recap: 1) Lina runs bench with StellarPay corpus (Priya/Omar to send sample), 2) Samir to send revised 12-month quote at 20% with bench acceptance clause, 3) legal addendum with data residency + KMS specifics, 4) target sign by Oct 15 to meet provision by Oct 31. any objections?
[36:30] Jason: no objections. we'll move forward.
[36:34] Priya: thanks everyone.
[36:36] Elena: thanks.
[36:38] Samir: thanks team, we'll follow up via email and post artifacts in the deal folder.
[36:44] Meeting end.
